description: Fix ctrl+c shutdown, add daemon mode with -d flag, and dashboard stop button for ralf serve

items.user_story: As a developer, I can press ctrl+c and the server exits cleanly so that the port is freed immediately
items.description: Fix the cleanup function in serve.ts to terminate all WebSocket connections, call process.exit(), log shutdown messages, and support double ctrl+c for force-kill
items.end_state: Pressing ctrl+c logs 'Shutting down...' and exits within 2 seconds. A second ctrl+c force-kills immediately. The port is freed and no orphan processes remain.
steps_to_verify: Run `ralf serve` and press ctrl+c — process exits and logs 'Shutting down...'
Run `ralf serve`, connect a browser to the dashboard, press ctrl+c — process still exits cleanly
Run `ralf serve` and press ctrl+c twice rapidly — process exits immediately on second press

items.user_story: As a developer, I can see the server PID in the config so I know whether the server is running
items.description: Add optional serve_pid field to RalfieConfig in shared types. Write PID to config on server start, clear it on shutdown.
items.end_state: RalfieConfig has an optional serve_pid: number | null field. When the server starts, config.json contains the PID. When it stops, serve_pid is null or absent.
steps_to_verify: Start `ralf serve`, check `.ralfie/config.json` contains `serve_pid` matching the process PID
Stop the server (ctrl+c), check `.ralfie/config.json` has `serve_pid: null`
Run `npm run typecheck` — no type errors in shared, cli, or ui workspaces

items.user_story: As a developer, I can run `ralf serve -d` to start the server in the background so my terminal stays free
items.description: Add -d/--daemon flag to the serve command. When set, fork a detached child process running the server, save its PID to config, print the PID, and exit the parent.
items.end_state: `ralf serve -d` prints the PID and returns to the shell prompt. The server runs in the background serving HTTP and WebSocket. The PID is saved in config.json.
steps_to_verify: Run `ralf serve -d` — command prints PID and returns to shell
Verify the printed PID is a running process: `ps -p <pid>`
Verify dashboard is accessible at http://localhost:3333

items.user_story: As a developer, I can run `ralf serve --stop` or `ralf serve -s` to kill the daemon from the terminal
items.description: Add --stop/-s flag to the serve command. Reads serve_pid from config, verifies the process exists, sends SIGTERM, clears serve_pid from config, and prints confirmation.
items.end_state: `ralf serve -s` kills the daemon, clears serve_pid from config, and prints a confirmation message. If no server is running, it prints a helpful message instead of crashing.
steps_to_verify: Start daemon with `ralf serve -d`, then run `ralf serve -s` — process is killed
Run `ralf serve -s` with no server running — prints 'No server running' without error
Run `ralf serve -s` with a stale PID in config — handles gracefully

items.user_story: As a developer, I can see the server PID and stop the server from the dashboard so I don't need the terminal
items.description: Add a POST /api/server/stop endpoint that triggers graceful shutdown. On the Settings page, display the server PID and a 'Stop Server' button that calls this endpoint.
items.end_state: Settings page shows the server PID in a status section. A red 'Stop Server' button calls POST /api/server/stop. The server shuts down gracefully after the response is sent.
steps_to_verify: Start `ralf serve -d` and open the Settings page — PID is displayed
Click 'Stop Server' — server shuts down, dashboard disconnects
Verify `.ralfie/config.json` has `serve_pid: null` after dashboard stop
The API function for stopping is exported from ui/src/lib/api.ts
